claims.text: The specified medium-pressure HVAF-i7 configuration will overcome the coating-thickness limitation previously observed with the 15–45 μm feedstock.
The intervention will produce an approximately 150 μm thick FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
The intervention will retain low coating porosity and minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The proposed FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 5–30 μm.
The feedstock contains microsegregated Al-rich and Cr-rich regions.
The feedstock forms a BCC random solid solution.
The grit-blasted Inconel 718 substrate has a roughness of Ra 3.9 ± 0.6 μm.
Earlier HVAF-i7 deposition with 15–45 μm feedstock produced acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
Low- and high-air/fuel-pressure settings produced coatings with 0.8–1.8% porosity.
Low- and high-air/fuel-pressure settings had lower deposition efficiencies than the medium-pressure setting.
The intervention will produce a coating with approximately 0.2% porosity.
The deposited coating will have a uniform elemental distribution and retain the BCC random-solid-solution structure.
The coating-substrate interdiffusion zone will be approximately 3 μm thick.
High-temperature oxidation will form a thin, dense, continuous Al2O3 thermally grown oxide with limited mixed-oxide formation.
The low-temperature HVAF-i7 process minimizes in-flight and deposition-stage oxidation.
Low coating porosity restricts oxygen ingress.
Outward diffusion of Al during high-temperature exposure facilitates formation of a protective alumina scale.
Sluggish elemental diffusion in the HEA reduces further oxide transport.
The FeCoNiCrAl coating lacks reactive elements, so oxidation protection depends on process control and coating density.
Relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, the intervention will improve deposition efficiency, reduce porosity, and improve oxidation resistance during 50 h exposures at 1000–1150 °C.
